raw.text:
🚨 DOCTORS JUST LOWERED “NORMAL” BLOOD PRESSURE AGAIN — AND PEOPLE ARE STARTING TO QUESTION EVERYTHING

In the 1970s, 160/95 was considered acceptable.  
Then it became 140/90.  
Now they’re pushing optimal all the way down to 110/70.  

Did our bodies suddenly change… or did the definition just keep moving?  

A growing number of voices are saying high blood pressure is often not the real disease. 

It’s the body’s compensation for deeper problems like insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction. 

Some studies even show that pushing numbers too low can increase the risk of heart attacks, kidney decline, and dementia... especially in older people.  

Most doctors are still only treating the number on the screen. Almost none are measuring the actual root causes.  

Are they actually helping people… or are they just creating more lifelong patients?

A single night of 4 hour sleep can drop insulin sensitivity by up to 25%.

Your body handles carbs worse, stores more fat, and spikes glucose longer. Chronic poor sleep can lead to prediabetes.

What to do:
+ Prioritize 7.5+ hrs of sleep
+ Eat earlier (at least 4 hrs before bed)
+ No coffee 6 hours before bed
+ No heavy exercise 4 hours before bed
+ Keep your room dark and cool
+ Avoid blue light and screens 1–2 hrs before sleep

- Para casos graves (sobrepeso severo, diabetes tipo 2): ayuno de 48 horas una vez por semana o OMAD (una comida al día) durante 9 días → ayuno de agua de 3 días cada 9 días...
Durante los ayunos con agua pura se permite: café negro, té negro, agua con electrolitos (por ejemplo, Element o ½ cucharadita de sal celta al día). ¿Antojos? 1 cucharadita de aceite MCT en agua...
Tuvo un paciente que ayunó 183 días (de 400 → a 210 libras) sin ningún problema de piel flácida, una "fisiología totalmente diferente" a la de la restricción calórica...
Dr. Pradip Jamnadas.

raw.author: CMEINDIA1
raw.text:
The Glucose Management Indicator (GMI) is a metric derived from Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) data that estimates a person’s laboratory-measured HbA1c. While GMI estimates A1C based on average glucose levels from 14+ days of sensor data, it is not identical to laboratory A1C, which measures blood sugar attached to red blood cells over 120 days. 

Key GMI & CGM Insights:

Purpose: GMI replaced "estimated A1C" (eA1C) to indicate current glucose control based on CGM data, rather than predicting the exact lab-tested result

GMI vs. A1C

 A lower GMI than lab A1C means the average CGM glucose is higher than predicted; a higher GMI than lab A1C suggests the average CGM glucose is lower than predicted.

Key Differences: 

GMI is based on daily glucose averages, whereas HbA1c is influenced by red blood cell lifespan.

Accuracy: 

While useful, GMI can differ from A1C due to rapid fluctuations, averaging 0.12–0.14 percentage points difference, though it can vary.

Usage: 
GMI is found on all standard CGM summary reports to guide diabetes management. 

GMI is generally considered more useful for evaluating recent glycemic trends (over 2 weeks) than laboratory HbA1c, which looks back over 3 months.

raw.author: JohnsonThomasMD
raw.text:
What if we treated high glucose not by giving a drug, but by removing glucose itself?

A study in Science this week describes ECHO, an implantable device designed to do exactly that, without insulin and without medication.

How it works:

The implant sits under the skin and contains an electrocatalyst made of platinum decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in porous graphite.

When wirelessly powered at low power (0.75 volts), the catalyst selectively converts blood glucose into gluconate. Gluconate carries less energy and is cleared by the kidneys into the urine, so both glucose and calories leave the body.

Because the reaction is driven electrically, the rate of glucose removal is adjustable. Turn the current up, remove glucose faster. Turn it off, removal stops.

The closed loop comes from pairing it with a standard continuous glucose monitor. The CGM detects glucose above a set threshold, the implant activates, glucose falls, and the system switches off. In this study it was also smartphone controlled.

What happened in mice with type 2 diabetes and obesity:

Glucose returned to the normal range within 1 hour of activation. Repeated treatment maintained control for 6 weeks with no detectable hypoglycemia. As glucose was removed, metabolism shifted toward fat use. Body weight and triglycerides fell, while free fatty acids and ketone bodies rose. No adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects were detected over those 6 weeks.

This is early stage, mice only, 6 weeks of data. Human questions are unanswered: catalyst durability over years, tissue reaction to a permanent implant, kidney handling of a sustained gluconate load, and whether the glucose removal rate scales from a mouse to a human.

We already have effective human therapies with outcome data, from metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors to GLP-1 receptor agonists and automated insulin delivery. ECHO is not a replacement for any of them today.

It is a proof of concept for a different category: closed loop diabetes care that does not deliver a drug at all, but removes the substrate itself. https://t.co/0DOdZyHWpo

raw.author: WilliamWallace
raw.text:
Most people assume that bringing down blood sugar after a meal takes a real workout, something like a brisk half hour or a trip to the gym. The research says the amount of movement needed is far smaller than that, and when you move matters even more than how long.

The reason sits in your muscles. When a muscle contracts, it pulls sugar out of the blood without needing insulin to open the door. The protein that carries the sugar in, called GLUT4, rises to the surface of the muscle cell in response to two separate signals, and muscle contraction is one of them. That is why movement lowers blood sugar even in people whose insulin works poorly, and why the effect shows up within minutes instead of after weeks of training.

A 2026 trial tested how little movement it takes. Thirty adults came in on two evenings and drank a standard sugar drink with 75 grams of glucose. On one evening they stayed seated, and on the other they stepped up and down stairs for a single minute at whatever pace felt comfortable. They rated the effort 1.9 out of 10, barely more than sitting. In the hour after the drink, their blood sugar rose about 42 percent less after the minute of stairs than after sitting, and their total sugar exposure across the session was lower too. The researchers chose the evening on purpose, because the same amount of sugar pushes blood sugar higher at night than it does in the morning.

One minute is right at the edge of what works, and it does not work in every situation. The same research group ran the comparison in the morning with bouts of 1, 3 and 10 minutes after the sugar drink. Three and ten minutes lowered blood sugar, while one minute did not come close to making a difference. When they repeated it after a real mixed meal of 650 calories, one minute did help, trimming the blood sugar rise by about 14 points on a standard glucose meter. So a single minute seems to be enough after a normal meal and in the evening, but not reliably after a morning sugar drink. Three minutes worked in every version they tested, which makes three the safer number to aim for.

Timing turned out to matter more than length. A 2023 analysis pooled eight trials with 116 people, about 4 in 10 of whom had type 2 diabetes, and compared exercising before a meal, after a meal, and not at all. Moving after the meal beat moving before it and beat doing nothing. Moving before the meal worked no better than sitting still. The analysis also found that the shorter the gap between finishing the meal and starting to move, the bigger the benefit, so a short walk taken right away does more than a longer one taken an hour later.

The useful change is in the ten minutes after you finish eating. Sitting down is what most of us do by default, and for blood sugar it is one of the weakest choices available. Climb the stairs if you have them or take a walk if you do not, and keep in mind that starting sooner matters more than going longer.

References
Morales et al., Experimental Physiology, 2026
Moore et al., Journal of Exercise Science and Fitness, 2024
Kressler et al., Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases, 2022
Engeroff et al., Sports Medicine, 2023

生酮饮食原本是用来治疗癫痫的，但科学家发现它可以治愈糖尿病、老年痴呆症、精神分裂症、抑郁、自闭症等等

酮体是一种清洁燃料，当你的大脑从燃烧葡萄糖切换到冉手酮，大脑的修复系统就被激活了。

很多人认为生酮饮食就是不吃碳水多吃肉。但实际上生酮的关键在于足够的脂肪，饮食比例中要达到65%-75%的脂肪。比如橄榄油、鳄梨油、坚果油、猪油、黄油等等。

糖和淀粉是目前饮食的大问题。高碳水饮食导致葡萄糖过量，导致胰岛素抵抗，导致一系列的代谢问题。本质上就是你的身体失去了自我调节的能力，所以血糖剧烈波动。

当你生酮时，身体就可以修复新陈代谢功能的障碍，提高胰岛素敏感性。

长期饮食不需要那么极端，你可以保持低碳，但不需要完全生酮。事实上只要你从胰岛素抵抗中恢复过来，你就会发现低碳和轻断食是一个自然而然的选择，因为你根本不容易饥饿，更不会低血糖，你对食物的欲望也没有那么强烈了。

但如果你有2型糖尿病或者其他严重疾病，作为治疗，你需要坚持严格生酮几个月，等到代谢机能恢复。

想了解更多生酮和低碳饮食的信息，关注我的账号。

raw.title: AI vibe coding 的进展，不知道程序员还能存活多久？
raw.content:
我那开劳斯莱斯的朋友，7 月份时候还是 coding 白痴， 但经过几个月的 vibe coding, 现在已经成功上线了工厂的 erp ，并且是那种可以当生产力工具用的，且按照他的说法，简直完美的和他工厂所有流程吻合。他正在慢慢的把周边模块一点一点的加上，不断的接入周边硬件，基本上都是许愿式的提交需求，大部分一次可以搞定。

而最关键的是，他已经知道利用 github actions 通过 Claude 做自动化部署实施，前 2 个月他还孤军奋战，现在他在 erp 中做了 issue/function request 提交界面，员工可以在该页面上直接提交到 github issue 中，他只是在 erp （可以直接看到 issues 所有状态）中看下员工提交的 issues, 判断后批准 Claude 直接接手进行修改代码经 github actions 自动部署的全自动化流程，拒绝则直接打回不执行，但有了 issue 记录，未来也可以进行回顾和评估。 

本来 Claude 搞完后还有个测试和预览过程，但这几个月他发现 Claude 做这种应用类软件，杀鸡用牛刀，所以取消了这个环节，反正现在整个框架和流程已经基本确定，所做的也只是一些小的修改和完善，无非是配色，布局，拼写错误之类的修改。

目前他已经进入到下一阶段，本地部署大模型（已经组装了算力服务器，虽然配置不太高，但基本工厂企业使用也最多是简单的 coding/视频图像处理）， 看是否可以替代 Claude code ，正在进行测试。也同时在评估工厂内部部署 gitlab 之类支持 github actions/runner 之类软件，达到未来实现全流程内部封闭运行，不依靠任何外部服务。

我会有空过来说下进度，各位有问题也可以提，因为他这个项目基本是我引导进行，相信会给你一些少走弯路的建议。

我那开劳斯莱斯的朋友，7 月份时候还是 coding 白痴， 但经过几个月的 vibe coding, 现在已经成功上线了工厂的 erp ，并且是那种可以当生产力工具用的，且按照他的说法，简直完美的和他工厂所有流程吻合。他正在慢慢的把周边模块一点一点的加上，不断的接入周边硬件，基本上都是许愿式的提交需求，大部分一次可以搞定。

而最关键的是，他已经知道利用 github actions 通过 Claude 做自动化部署实施，前 2 个月他还孤军奋战，现在他在 erp 中做了 issue/function request 提交界面，员工可以在该页面上直接提交到 github issue 中，他只是在 erp （可以直接看到 issues 所有状态）中看下员工提交的 issues, 判断后批准 Claude 直接接手进行修改代码经 github actions 自动部署的全自动化流程，拒绝则直接打回不执行，但有了 issue 记录，未来也可以进行回顾和评估。

本来 Claude 搞完后还有个测试和预览过程，但这几个月他发现 Claude 做这种应用类软件，杀鸡用牛刀，所以取消了这个环节，反正现在整个框架和流程已经基本确定，所做的也只是一些小的修改和完善，无非是配色，布局，拼写错误之类的修改。

目前他已经进入到下一阶段，本地部署大模型（已经组装了算力服务器，虽然配置不太高，但基本工厂企业使用也最多是简单的 coding/视频图像处理）， 看是否可以替代 Claude code ，正在进行测试。也同时在评估工厂内部部署 gitlab 之类支持 github actions/runner 之类软件，达到未来实现全流程内部封闭运行，不依靠任何外部服务。

我会有空过来说下进度，各位有问题也可以提，因为他这个项目基本是我引导进行，相信会给你一些少走弯路的建议。
